subject: US privacy addendum / service provider language - subprocessor notice timing
messages:
From: Allison Brown <allison.brown@acme-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: US privacy addendum - service provider language & subprocessor list

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of privacy items before we can move forward with the pilot:

1) We need a US-state privacy addendum (CCPA/CPRA + other state clauses) that uses a "service provider / processor" construct rather than a "controller/controller" model. We have a few specific asks below.
2) We need a list of subprocessors (current + onboarding process). Procurement prefers a 10-day notice before onboarding and the ability to object.
3) Data residency: Acme requires that customer data for US accounts remain within the US unless otherwise agreed. Can you confirm where Redwood routes inference requests and any persistent logs?

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and a sample addendum (Acme_DPA_questions_20251103.pdf).

High-level timeline: we need the signed addendum by end of November to hit our Q4 pilot start. Can you let me know the next steps?

Thanks,
Allison Brown
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_DPA_questions_20251103.pdf (pdf, 98KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: US privacy addendum - service provider language & subprocessor list

Hi Allison — thanks for the note and the attachments. Great to hear the pilot timeline.

We're happy to operate as a service provider/processor for Acme's deployment. Looping in Priya (legal) and Karthik (platform) to propose a draft addendum and confirm operational details. A couple quick answers while they prepare the doc:

- Data residency: by default, Redwood routes inference and ephemeral caches to the region you select; for hosted US tenants we keep data in US regions unless you opt into cross-region backup/replication. Any persistent logs kept for billing/observability are stored in US for US accounts unless otherwise requested.
- Subprocessors: we publish a current subprocessor list and a notification process. Standard proposal is 30 days prior notice and opportunity to object for customers.

Priya/Karthik — can you review Acme's questionnaire and the attached sample and propose redlines for a US-state addendum that focuses on service provider obligations (CCPA/CPRA, and other state frameworks that use similar "sale/service provider" language)? If we can get draft redlines back by EOD tomorrow we can share with Allison and her procurement team.

Next steps: draft redlines -> shared Drive link -> procurement review -> DocuSign (if agreed).

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposed US Privacy Addendum - redlines

Monica / Karthik,

Attached are redlines for a US-state privacy addendum oriented around a "Service Provider / Processor" relationship (Redwood_US_Addendum_Redline_20251104.docx). Key points and suggested compromise positions:

1) Processor role: we accept express processor/service provider language. We add clarifying language that Redwood processes Personal Information only to provide the Services and per documented instructions.

2) "Sale" / Consumer Rights: for CCPA/CPRA, we will adopt the standard definition that a "sale" does not include a bona fide service provider forwarding of data to subprocessors necessary to provide the service. We will include a carve-out for operational telemetry used strictly for billing/quality (pseudonymized where feasible).

3) Subprocessors: proposed workflow:
   - Redwood will keep an up-to-date public subprocessor register.
   - For routine additions, Redwood will provide 30 calendar days' notice before onboarding. Customer may object within that 30-day period; if objection is reasonable and results in a prohibited risk, Redwood will work in good faith to remove the subprocessor or propose a mitigant.
   - For critical security patches or emergency failover (e.g., replacing a compromised infra provider), Redwood may onboard a subprocessor with shorter notice (14 days) but will notify immediately and provide remediation options.
   - For expressly prohibited subprocessors per customer policy, Redwood will refuse or provide a commercial workaround.

4) Removal and cure: requestors often ask for "immediate removal" rights. We propose: upon a legitimate objection that cannot be mitigated, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to disengage the subprocessor within 30 days; if data cannot be returned it will be deleted/sanitized as agreed. For high-risk (e.g., law enforcement or DOJ access concerns) we can negotiate special terms.

5) Data residency and transfers: for US customers, default storage/processing will be within US regions. If cross-border processing is required (e.g., a non-US subprocessor), we will rely on appropriate transfer safeguards and will disclose transfers in the subprocessor register.

6) Evidence and audit: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and respond to limited security questionnaires. We can provide a read-only audit portal for enterprise customers at higher tiers.

7) Indemnity and liability: retain standard liability caps aligned to the services agreement; no open-ended indemnity for privacy claims.

I've included an embedded redline with tracked changes and brief comment boxes explaining rationale. If Acme pushes for 10-day notice and immediate removal, we should be prepared to: (a) offer a 14-day notice for routine additions, (b) offer 7-day expedited notice only for a commercial fee or higher support tier, or (c) accept 10-day notice for a limited category of subprocessors that are low-risk (analytics, monitoring).

Action items:
- Monica: please confirm whether Acme would accept 30/14 compromise or needs 10/Immediate as a hardline.
- Karthik: please confirm whether 14-day emergency onboarding timeline is operationally feasible for platform ops and whether we can provide an interim mitigation (e.g., temporary isolated environment).

Attachment: Redwood_US_Addendum_Redline_20251104.docx (docx, 24KB)

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Allison Brown <allison.brown@acme-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: US privacy addendum - service provider language & subprocessor list

Monica / Priya — thanks for the fast turnaround and the redlines. Procurement reviewed and had a couple of follow-ups: 

1) Notice timing: Acme's security policy requires a maximum 10-calendar-day notice for any new subprocessor onboarding; for any subprocessor that will host or persist customer data we need the ability to require removal within 7 calendar days if remediation is not acceptable. Is Redwood willing to accept 10-day notice and a 7-day removal window for subprocessors that handle persisted customer data?

2) Emergency onboarding: we appreciate the 14-day emergency path. For critical outages, we can accept emergency onboarding with immediate notification but will require a post-implementation remediation plan and a 7-day demonstration of compensation measures.

3) Evidence: please provide a link to the most recent SOC2 report and a completed Vendor Security Questionnaire (we attached ours for reference).

4) Next steps: procurement would like the updated redline reflecting the 10-day / 7-day positions and a final addendum we can sign via DocuSign. Please also attach the subprocessor register.

We are aiming to execute the addendum by Nov 28 to meet our pilot kickoff.

Thanks,
Allison Brown
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics
